He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. As a senior, he was named [[Mr. Basketball USA]] and the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award]]. ==High school career== Whitehead attended [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]].{{cite magazine|first=Jason|last=Jordan|title=Southern JamFest: Dariq Whitehead Reminding the Masses He's the [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award]] his senior year in 2022.{{cite web|first=Adam|last=Zagoria|title=Newark native, Duke pledge Dariq Whitehead named Naismith Boys' High School Player of the Year|url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2022/03/newark-native-duke-pledge-dariq-whitehead-named-naismith-boys-high-school-player-of-the-year.html|website=nj.com|date=March 4, in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].{{cite magazine|first=Shawn|last=Krest|title=Three Jon Scheyer Recruits Named McDonald's named the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] MVP, where he had 13 points, seven rebounds, and seven assists.{{cite web |date=March 30, 2022 |title=Villanova, Duke recruits star in McDonald's game |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33627246 |access-date=March 31, 2022 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} Whitehead was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. career== On November 18, 2022, Whitehead made his [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] debut recording 6 points, 2 rebounds and 2 steals in 16 minutes off the bench in a 92–58 win against [[Delaware Fightin' Blue Hens men's basketball|Delaware]].{{cite web|title=Whitehead makes collegiate debut in Duke win|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35054557/duke-freshman-dariq-whitehead-makes-collegiate-debut-vs-delaware|website=ESPN.com|date=November 18, 2022|access-date=December 21, 2024}} On December 6, 2022, Whitehead scored eight points and set a career-high six rebounds and three assists in 21 minutes off the bench in a 74–62 win against [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]]. On December 10, 2022, Whitehead made his first college career start scoring 15 points in 25 minutes of action in an 82–55 win against [[Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks men's basketball|UMES]] which also marked the first time Duke started five freshmen in program history. On January 7, 2023, Whitehead scored a career high 18 points and 33 minutes played and matching previously set career highs in 6 field goals made and 4 3-pointers made, while shooting 50% (6-of-12) from the field and 50% (4-of-8) from long range during a 65–64 win against [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]]. On February 18, 2023, Whitehead made a career-high-tying four 3-pointers (4-of-6) en route to 14 points with a career-high-tying three assists and two steals during a 77–55 win against [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] marking his eighth time scoring in double figures in an 11-game span. On March 10, 2023, Whitehead recorded 16 points in 19 minutes against [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]] on 3/10 in the [[ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC Tournament]] semifinals on 4-of-8 shooting, including 2-of-3 shooting from beyond the arc. On March 11, 2023, Whitehead logged four steals off the bench in the ACC title game in a 59–49 win against [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]], matching the most by any Duke player in a game during the 2022–23 season. In two NCAA Tournament games, Whitehead recorded averages of 10.5 points on .615 shooting from the field and .625 shooting from distance with 3.0 rebounds in 28.0 minutes per contest... Scored 13 points (5-of-7 FG, 3-of-3 3FG) in 23 minutes off the bench in Duke's NCAA Tournament win against Oral Roberts. Played a career-high-tying 33 minutes in Duke's second-round NCAA Tournament game against Tennessee, posting eight points (3-of-6 FG, 2-of-5 3FG) with two rebounds and a career-high-tying two blocks. ==Professional career== === Brooklyn Nets (2023–2025) === The [[Brooklyn Nets]] selected Whitehead with the 22nd overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]]{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Select Noah Clowney, Dariq Whitehead and Jalen Wilson in 2023 NBA Draft|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-select-noah-clowney-dariq-whitehead-and-jalen-wilson-in-2023-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 23, 2023|access-date=December 23, 2024}} and on July 10, 2023, he signed with the team.{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Dariq Whitehead|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-dariq-whitehead|website=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2023|access-date=December 23, 2024}} Throughout his rookie and sophomore seasons, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Long Island Nets]].{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Long Island Nets Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Long-Island-Nets/46/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 23, during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 1.5 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dariq Whitehead 2023-24 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432735/type/nba/year/2024|access-date=December 27, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} Whitehead made 20 appearances for the Nets during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], posting averages of 5.7 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 0.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dariq Whitehead 2024-25 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4432735/type/nba/year/2025|access-date=December 27, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}} On October 13, 2025, Whitehead, alongside [[Drew Timme]], was waived from the Nets.{{cite web |last1=Helwig |first1=Collin |title=Brooklyn Nets cut Dariq Whitehead and Drew Timme (who may be back) |url=https://www.netsdaily.com/nets-news/99974/brooklyn-nets-cut-dariq-whitehead-and-drew-timme |website=NetsDaily |access-date=October 25, 2025 |date=October 13, 2025}} === Oklahoma City Blue
